question: How can we develop effective personalized systems to improve understanding of scientific concepts and jargon across different domains and expertise levels?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must propose combining a plasmonic nanoparticle (e.g., gold nanorod/nanostar) with an optical microcavity (e.g., whispering gallery mode microsphere/microtoroid or photonic crystal resonance) as the core sensing platform.
examples: Coupling a gold nanostar to a photonic crystal guided resonance
A metal nanoparticle bound to the surface of a WGM microtoroid biosensor
Hybrid photonic-plasmonic resonator consisting of an MNP and a WGM microcavity

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify that the nanoparticle's localized surface plasmon resonance strongly enhances the local electric field at the analyte binding site, increasing the resonant frequency shift upon molecular binding.
examples: Nanorod tips give field enhancements in excess of 10^3 near resonance
LSPR of the AuNR amplifies the frequency shift by ~870x for a single BSA molecule
MNP offers a highly enhanced local field in the vicinity of an emitter

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer must explain that the microcavity confines light in a high-Q whispering gallery mode that forms a localized resonance highly sensitive to refractive index changes at the sensor surface.
examples: WGM traps an oscillating mode sensitive to surface refractive index change
High-Q property of WGMs is maintained even in the presence of the MNP
Microtoroid resonator supports high-Q modes for biosensing

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must state that spatial and spectral overlap between the nanoparticle's LSPR and the cavity's WGM leads to hybridization and cooperatively enhanced light-matter interaction.
examples: Resonantly enhanced polarizability of the nanorod scatters light back into the microtoroid, splitting WGMs into a doublet
WGM-LSPR hybridization boosts single-atom cooperativity by more than two orders of magnitude
Coupling to a photonic crystal guided resonance produces an ultrasharp Lorentzian hybrid resonance

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer must quantify that the hybrid approach amplifies the resonance wavelength/frequency shift or light-matter interaction by orders of magnitude relative to the bare cavity or bare nanoparticle alone.
examples: Single BSA molecule frequency shift increased by a factor of 870
Single-atom cooperativity enhanced by more than two orders of magnitude vs bare WGM cavity
One-order-of-magnitude amplified absorption in the nanoantenna

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer should note that the hybrid retains the cavity's high Q-factor while adding the nanoparticle's nanoscale mode volume, overcoming limitations of either component alone.
examples: High-Q WGM property maintained despite the MNP
Deep subwavelength mode volume together with high Q-factor in buffer
Hybrid system has advantages over a single microcavity or single MNP

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer should mention a design or modeling principle for the hybrid system, such as coupled-mode theory or achieving maximum power transfer under critical coupling.
examples: Coupled mode model reveals cavity-mediated activation of nanoantennas
Maximum power transferred to antennas attained under critical coupling
Linewidth of the enhancement widely tunable

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer should acknowledge limitations such as nanoparticle absorption reducing the cavity Q-factor or destructive Fano interference rendering the antenna transparent.
examples: Absorption from the nanorod reduces the Q factor of the resonator
Antenna can be rendered transparent by the cavity through destructive Fano interference
Matching low mode volume with long photon storage time remains challenging
